question: What is 'Sacred Tradition' in Catholic teaching — is it just old customs, or something more?

choices.A: It is the living transmission of the Gospel through the Church's life, worship, and teaching — part of the one deposit of faith alongside Scripture
choices.B: It is a collection of human customs that may be changed whenever the pope decides
choices.C: It refers only to ancient liturgical rites and has no doctrinal content
choices.D: It is the oral teachings of the apostles written down in the second century only

teaching.title: Sacred Tradition
teaching.body: Vatican II's Dei Verbum (1965) defined Sacred Tradition as the apostolic preaching handed on through the Holy Spirit in the Church's life, worship, and teaching. It is not a second, separate source added to Scripture, but both flow from the same divine spring (Christ) and together form one deposit of faith. Sacred Tradition includes: the creeds, liturgical practices, the canon of Scripture itself, and the consistent teaching of the Magisterium. It is 'living' in that it can be understood more deeply over time — this is doctrinal development (Newman's thesis), not change.
